sinusoidal_pe.Why do transformers need positional info: Attention is permutation-equivariant. Without positions, "dog bites man" and "man bites dog" look the same.
sinusoidal_pe.How does the sinusoidal encoding work, a: Each pair of dimensions is a sinusoid at a different frequency, like the hands of a clock or binary digits, from fast to slow.
sinusoidal_pe.Write out the formula. Which dimensions: PE(p, 2i) = sin(p / 10000^(2i/d)) and PE(p, 2i+1) = cos(same). Even dims get sin, odd dims get cos.
sinusoidal_pe.Why can a fixed linear transformation ma: For each frequency the pair (sin, cos) at p + k is a rotation of the pair at p, and the rotation depends only on k.
sinusoidal_pe.How do you compute it without a Python l: Build positions (S, 1) and frequencies (1, d/2), multiply, then fill the even and odd columns with sin and cos.
sinusoidal_pe.Sinusoidal versus learned absolute posit: Compare parameters, extrapolation and whether relative position appears directly in the attention score.
sinusoidal_pe.Why do absolute encodings extrapolate po: The model never saw those positions during training. Learned tables have no entries for them, and the sinusoid combinations are unseen.

rope.What is RoPE, and why does rotating Q an: It rotates Q and K pairs by a position-dependent angle. The dot product of two rotated vectors depends only on the angle difference.
rope.Why is RoPE applied to Q and K but not V: Position only has to affect which keys match which queries. V carries content that should be mixed as-is.
rope.Walk through pairing dimensions and appl: Pair dimensions (2i, 2i+1) or the two halves. theta_i = base^(-2i/d). Rotate each pair by position times theta_i.
rope.Interleaved pairs versus half-split pair: Interleaved pairs (original paper, GPT-J, Meta's LLaMA code) versus half-split (GPT-NeoX, Hugging Face LLaMA, which permutes Meta's q/k weights). Mixing conventions pairs the wrong dimensions and scrambles positions.
rope.How do you apply RoPE with a KV cache wh: Rotate new tokens at their absolute positions (offset plus index) and cache the rotated keys.
rope.Why does RoPE degrade beyond the trainin: Low-frequency dims never completed a full rotation during training, so longer positions produce unseen angles.
rope.RoPE versus ALiBi: extrapolation and eff: ALiBi adds a linear distance bias inside the attention scores, extrapolates somewhat but always penalizes long range. RoPE is applied to Q and K before attention, so any kernel works unchanged, with comparable or slightly better quality at the training length.

alibi.What is ALiBi, and how does it replace p: It adds a per-head bias to the attention logits proportional to query-key distance, with no position embeddings at all.
alibi.Why does ALiBi extrapolate to longer seq: The bias is a simple function of distance that keeps working past the training length, since it only makes far tokens less likely.
alibi.How are head slopes computed, and why ge: Slopes 2^(-8/n), 2^(-16/n) and so on. A geometric range gives heads from local to near-global focus.
alibi.How do you build the bias matrix and com: bias = -slope * (i - j) for j <= i. Add it to the logits together with -inf for future positions.
alibi.Where exactly is the bias added?: On the pre-softmax logits after the QK^T scaling, per head.
alibi.What does ALiBi's linear recency bias co: Far tokens are always penalized, which hurts retrieval of distant facts. Mention needle-in-a-haystack results.
alibi.Why did most recent LLMs pick RoPE over: RoPE fits well into existing kernels and gives better quality at the training length. Long context was then solved by RoPE scaling methods.

ntk_rope.Why does plain RoPE fail beyond the trai: Positions past training produce rotation angles the model never saw, especially in the low-frequency dimensions.
ntk_rope.What does NTK-aware scaling do different: Linear interpolation squeezes all positions, losing high-frequency resolution. NTK changes the base so high frequencies stay nearly intact.
ntk_rope.How is the base adjusted from the scale: base' = base * s^(d / (d - 2)). Derive it by requiring the lowest frequency to be interpolated by s.
ntk_rope.Why are high-frequency dimensions preser: High frequencies encode local order, which the model relies on. Low frequencies encode long range and need stretching to cover new lengths.
ntk_rope.What stays unchanged when scale equals o: With s = 1 the base is unchanged, so the output equals plain RoPE.
ntk_rope.NTK scaling versus YaRN versus fine-tuni: NTK needs no training but is imperfect. YaRN adds per-band ramps and an attention temperature. Fine-tuning is best but costs compute and data.
ntk_rope.What quality regressions do you see on s: Changed frequencies slightly shift short-range behavior. Look for perplexity increases at the original length. Dynamic NTK avoids scaling short inputs.

causal_attention.Why do autoregressive models need a caus: At generation time, token t cannot see t+1. If training lets it peek, what does the model learn, and what happens at inference?
causal_attention.How does causal masking relate to teache: Teacher forcing feeds the ground-truth prefix for every position in one pass. The mask is what makes that one pass equal to S separate next-token predictions.
causal_attention.How do you build the mask, and why fill: Use an upper-triangular boolean mask above the diagonal. A zero logit still gets exp(0) = 1 weight; -inf gets exactly 0.
causal_attention.Why must masking happen before the softm: After softmax, zeroing weights leaves rows that no longer sum to 1. Masking the logits first renormalizes over the allowed positions.
causal_attention.What does the first row of the attention: Token 0 can only see itself, so its row is a one-hot on column 0.
causal_attention.How does causal attention enable KV cach: Past tokens never see future ones, so their keys and values never change. You can compute them once and reuse them.
causal_attention.Causal versus bidirectional attention: w: Bidirectional gives richer representations for understanding tasks (BERT). Causal enables generation and caching. Mention prefix-LM hybrids.

cross_attention.What is cross-attention, and where is it: Queries come from one sequence, keys and values from another. Name encoder-decoder translation, Whisper and text-to-image diffusion.
cross_attention.Which sequence provides Q and which prov: The decoder (the one being generated) provides Q; the encoder output or conditioning provides K and V.
cross_attention.How do shapes work when the query and ke: Q is (B, S_q, d) and K, V are (B, S_kv, d), so the scores are (B, S_q, S_kv) and the output has the query's length.
cross_attention.Why is there no causal mask here?: The encoder output is fully known before decoding starts, so there is no future to hide.
cross_attention.How would you add a padding mask for the: Build a (B, S_kv) mask for padded encoder positions, broadcast it over heads and queries, and fill with -inf before the softmax.
cross_attention.Cross-attention versus concatenating the: Concatenation costs (S_q + S_kv)^2 and mixes both ways. Cross-attention costs S_q * S_kv and keeps the roles separate.
cross_attention.How can you cache the K and V of cross-a: The encoder output does not change during decoding, so compute its K and V once and reuse them at every step.

gqa.What is grouped-query attention, and why: Several query heads share one K/V head. It was introduced to shrink the KV cache and memory bandwidth at decode time.
gqa.How does it sit between multi-head and m: MHA has as many KV heads as query heads; MQA has one. GQA uses G groups in between.
gqa.How do you expand KV heads to match quer: repeat_interleave copies each KV head adjacently (k0 k0 k1 k1), matching contiguous query groups; repeat tiles the heads (k0 k1 k0 k1). Use the one that matches the grouping.
gqa.What must divide what for the shapes to: The number of query heads must be divisible by the number of KV heads.
gqa.How much does GQA shrink the KV cache?: The cache shrinks by n_heads / n_kv_heads, for example 8x for 64 query heads and 8 KV heads.
gqa.What quality does GQA lose compared with: It shows a small quality drop versus MHA and less than MQA. Cite the GQA paper's uptraining results.
gqa.How would you convert a multi-head check: Mean-pool the K and V projection weights within each group, then uptrain for a small fraction of the original compute.

sliding_window.What is sliding-window attention, and wh: Each token attends only to the last w tokens. Cost becomes linear in length, and so does cache memory.
sliding_window.How can stacking layers extend the effec: Information hops w tokens per layer, so L layers see about L * w tokens. Think of receptive fields in CNNs.
sliding_window.How do you build the band mask?: Allowed when |i - j| <= w (plus j <= i for causal). Build it from broadcast index differences.
sliding_window.Does this exercise's window include both: Check whether j - i can be positive in this exercise. For causal, add the j <= i condition.
sliding_window.What is the complexity with and without: Dense with a mask is still O(S^2). A banded or blocked kernel gets O(S * w).
sliding_window.What long-range dependencies does a slid: Facts farther back than the effective receptive field. Hybrids interleave some global attention layers, for example Gemma 2 and 3 or gpt-oss.
sliding_window.How does a sliding window change KV cach: The cache only needs the last w entries, as a rolling buffer, instead of growing with length.

linear_attention.What is linear attention, and how does i: It replaces softmax with a kernel feature map so attention factorizes. Computing phi(K)^T V first costs O(S d^2).
linear_attention.What role does the feature map phi play?: phi maps queries and keys to non-negative features whose dot product approximates a similarity. It stands in for exp.
linear_attention.Show how reordering the matrix products: (phi(Q) phi(K)^T) V is S x S; phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V) is d x d. Matrix multiplication is associative.
linear_attention.Why must phi produce non-negative featur: Non-negative features keep the weights positive like softmax's. The normalizer phi(Q) times the sum of phi(K) makes the weights sum to 1.
linear_attention.How would you make linear attention caus: Keep a running state S_t = S_{t-1} + phi(k_t) v_t^T and a running normalizer z_t. It becomes an RNN.
linear_attention.Why does linear attention usually underp: The fixed-size state cannot store sharp, precise lookups; softmax can focus on a single key. Associative recall suffers.
linear_attention.How do modern state-space and linear RNN: Mamba, RetNet and GLA are linear attention with decay or gating on the state. Say what gating adds.

flash_attention.What problem does FlashAttention solve,: Memory traffic: the S x S matrix is written to and read from HBM. FlashAttention tiles the work in SRAM.
flash_attention.What is the online softmax trick?: Compute softmax block by block, keeping a running max and running sum, and rescale earlier partial results when the max grows.
flash_attention.Walk through how running max and running: For each new block: m_new = max(m, block max); l_new = l * exp(m - m_new) + sum of exp(scores - m_new).
flash_attention.How do you rescale the accumulated outpu: Multiply the accumulated output by exp(m_old - m_new) (and the ratio of normalizers) before adding the new block's contribution.
flash_attention.Why is the result exactly equal to stand: Rescaling makes every term end up with the same reference max, so the algebra matches softmax exactly, up to floating-point rounding.
flash_attention.What does FlashAttention do for the back: It stores only the output and the log-sum-exp, and recomputes the attention blocks in backward instead of saving the matrix.
flash_attention.When would FlashAttention not help much?: Very short sequences, tiny head dims, or when compute-bound. Also hardware without enough SRAM or unusual masks.
